Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

government noun

also the authorities, those in power, governing

classical

Cic. Fam. 1.8.4: iī, quī potiuntur rērum
Cic. Rosc. Am. 70: cīvitās Athēniēnsium, dum ea rērum potīta est (Lewis & Short)

quī rērum potiuntur

phrase: potior with the genitive

those in power, the government

Rērum potīrī is to hold power in the state (Lewis & Short); Cicero’s phrase for the men in power in his day.

Other words

  • rēs pūblica, reī pūblicae f. — the state; public affairs and their management

    noun, fifth declension, with an adjective · also used · classical · Traupman 179, 323; M-O s.v. government

    Traupman’s and Morgan–Owens’s first word for government; classically the commonwealth itself rather than the men who govern it.

  • magistrātūs, magistrātuum m. pl. — the magistrates, the authorities

    noun, fourth declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 63 (Lewis & Short)

    Properly the offices, then the men who hold them.

  • gubernātiō, gubernātiōnis f. — governing, the steering of a state

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 1.2: cīvitātis (Lewis & Short)

  • regimen, regiminis n. — rule, direction

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Tac. (Lewis & Short); Traupman 323; M-O s.v. government

    Post-Augustan, above all in Tacitus; not in Cicero or Caesar.

Examples

  • ōtium nōbīs exoptandum est, quod iī, quī potiuntur rērum, praestātūrī videntur

    we must hope for the peace and quiet that those in power seem ready to guaranteeCic. Fam. 1.8.4

See also state, political, policy.
